# simDAG

**Simulate complex data from explicit data-generating processes in R**

`simDAG` is an R package for generating synthetic data from directed
acyclic graphs (DAGs). Users specify how variables are generated and how
they depend on one another, and may then simulate datasets from the
resulting data-generating process (DGP).

Beyond ordinary cross-sectional data, `simDAG` supports complex
longitudinal processes, time-to-event outcomes, censoring, recurrent and
competing events, and dependencies between individuals through networks.
It additionally implements an enhanced `formula` interface, allowing
specifications of arbitrary interactions, non-linear effects,
dependencies on categorical variables and random effects. The
development version also supports calibrating conditional model
parameters to achieve user-defined target characteristics, including
marginal effects.

## Installation

Install the current CRAN release:

``` r

install.packages("simDAG")
```

To install the development version from GitHub, including the new
[`calibrate_dag()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/calibrate_dag.md)
functionality:

``` r

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("RobinDenz1/simDAG")
```

## Quick start

Suppose we want to generate data with a continuous covariate $`X`$, a
binary treatment $`A`$, and a binary outcome $`Y`$. Both treatment and
outcome depend on $`X`$, and the outcome also depends on treatment.

``` r

library(simDAG)

dag <- empty_dag() +
  node("X", type="rnorm", mean=0, sd=1) +
  node("A", type="binomial",
       formula= ~ -0.5 + X * 0.6) +
  node("Y", type= "binomial",
       formula= ~ -1 + A * 0.7 + X * 0.4)

set.seed(43)
data <- sim_from_dag(dag, n_sim=10000)
head(data)
#>              X      A      Y
#>          <num> <lgcl> <lgcl>
#> 1: -0.03751376  FALSE   TRUE
#> 2: -1.57460441  FALSE  FALSE
#> 3: -0.48596752   TRUE  FALSE
#> 4:  0.46518623   TRUE   TRUE
#> 5: -0.90409807  FALSE   TRUE
#> 6: -0.27743280   TRUE  FALSE
```

The DAG below represents the data-generating process: $`X`$ influences
both treatment ($`A`$) and outcome ($`Y`$), while $`A`$ also influences
$`Y`$.

![](reference/figures/README-dag-plot-1.png)

Each node is generated according to its specified distribution or
conditional model. The order of the nodes and their dependencies define
the data-generating process. The same approach extends to much more
complex DGPs, including custom generation functions and longitudinal
processes.

## What can you simulate?

| Use case | Main functionality |
|----|----|
| Cross-sectional data from a DAG | [`sim_from_dag()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/sim_from_DAG.md) |
| Longitudinal data with time-varying variables | [`sim_discrete_time()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/sim_discrete_time.md) |
| Continuous-time event-driven data | [`sim_discrete_event()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/sim_discrete_event.md) |
| Data with dependencies between individuals | [`network()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/network.md) functionality |
| Data with custom conditional models | Custom [`node()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/node.md) types and generation functions |
| Data with prespecified marginal characteristics | [`calibrate_dag()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/calibrate_dag.md) (development version) |

The package implements many node types for user convenience, including
linear-, logistic-, Poisson- and Cox-, regression models, among many
others. See
[`node()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/node.md) for an
overview.

### Cross-sectional data

Generate data from static DAGs containing continuous, binary,
categorical, count, and time-to-event variables. Nodes can be specified
using conditional distributions, regression models or custom functions.

**Learn more:** [Simulating Data from a Known
DAG](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/articles/v_sim_from_dag.html)

### Longitudinal data and survival processes

Use
[`sim_discrete_time()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/sim_discrete_time.md)
to generate complex longitudinal data with time-varying covariates,
time-dependent effects, censoring, recurrent events, and competing
events.

For suitable models,
[`sim_discrete_event()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/sim_discrete_event.md)
offers an alternative based on event-driven simulation in continuous
time. It can be considerably faster than discrete-time simulation,
although it supports a narrower range of time-dependent processes.

**Learn more:** [Discrete-time
simulation](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/articles/v_sim_discrete_time.html)
· [Discrete-event
simulation](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/articles/v_sim_discrete_event.html)

### Network-dependent data

`simDAG` also supports dependencies between individuals through static
and dynamic network structures, allowing the generated data to
incorporate network-based relationships.

**Learn more:** [Simulating Data from a DAG with Network
Dependencies](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/articles/v_sim_networks.html)

## Specify marginal targets instead of manually tuning coefficients

When defining a DGP through conditional models, the resulting marginal
characteristics are not always obvious. For example, specifying the
coefficients of a logistic regression model does not directly specify
the marginal prevalence of its outcome or the marginal causal effect of
treatment.

The
[`calibrate_dag()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/calibrate_dag.md)
function addresses this problem by allowing users to leave selected
parameters unspecified and determine them numerically so that
user-defined targets are achieved as closely as possible.

For example, suppose we want an outcome prevalence of 30%, while
retaining the specified relationships between treatment, a confounder,
and the outcome.

``` r

ldag <- lazy_dag(
  empty_dag() +
    node("X", type="rnorm", mean=0, sd=1) +
    node("A", type="binomial",
         formula= ~ -0.5 + X * 0.8) +
    node("Y", type= "binomial",
         formula= ~ param(intercept_Y) +
           A * 0.7 + X * 0.4)
)

targets <- list(
  prevalence_Y = list(
    target = 0.30,
    eval_fun = function(data) mean(data$Y)
  )
)

params <- list(
  intercept_Y = list(
    start = 0,
    range = c(-5, 5)
  )
)

fit <- calibrate_dag(
  lazy_dag = ldag,
  targets = targets,
  params = params,
  n_sim_run = 5000,
  n_sim_eval = 20000,
  seed = 42
)

summary(fit)
#> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> Calibrated DAG
#> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> Parameters (1)
#>    parameter estimate start lower upper parscale
#>  intercept_Y   -1.135     0    -5     5       NA
#> 
#> Targets (1)
#>        target desired achieved   error scaled_error
#>  prevalence_Y     0.3   0.3069 0.00685      0.00685
#> 
#> Optimization
#>   Method:       uniroot
#>   Convergence:  successful
#>   Root residual: 0
#>   Iterations:   8
#>   Simulations:  5,000 optimization; 20,000 final evaluation
#> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

The result includes the calibrated parameters, the achieved target
values, and optimization diagnostics. The resulting fully specified DAG
is available as `fit$dag` and can be used with the usual simulation
functions.

Calibration is numerical and approximate. Inspect the achieved target
values rather than relying solely on optimizer convergence.

**Learn more:** [Calibrating a DAG to Match Target
Characteristics](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/articles/v_calibrate_dag.html)

  reference](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/index.html)

introductory vignette and cookbook are good places to start.

If you use `simDAG` in your research, please cite:

Denz, R. and Timmesfeld, N. (2026). Simulating Complex Cross-Sectional
and Longitudinal Data using the simDAG R Package. *Journal of
Statistical Software*, 116(2). <https://doi.org/10.18637/jss.v116.i02>

# Package index

## DAGs

Create, manipulate and inspect DAGs

- [`empty_dag()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/empty_dag.md)
  :

  Initialize an empty `DAG` object

- [`node()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/node.md)
  [`node_td()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/node.md) :

  Create a node object for a `DAG`

- [`network()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/network.md)
  [`network_td()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/network.md)
  :

  Create a network object for a `DAG`

- [`net()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/net.md) :

  Specify Network Dependencies in a `DAG`

- [`add_node()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/add_node.md)
  [`` `+`( ``*`<DAG>`*`)`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/add_node.md)
  :

  Add a `DAG.node` or a `DAG.network` object to a `DAG` object

- [`lazy_dag()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/lazy_dag.md)
  :

  Define a partial `DAG` object without evaluating it

- [`set_lazy_dag()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/set_lazy_dag.md)
  :

  Create a fully defined `DAG` object from a `lazy_DAG` object

- [`plot(`*`<DAG>`*`)`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/plot.DAG.md)
  :

  Plot a `DAG` object

- [`as.igraph(`*`<DAG>`*`)`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/as.igraph.DAG.md)
  :

  Transform a `DAG` object into an `igraph` object

- [`as.dagitty(`*`<DAG>`*`)`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/as.dagitty.DAG.md)
  :

  Transform a `DAG` object into a `dagitty` object

- [`as_tidy_dagitty(`*`<DAG>`*`)`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/as_tidy_dagitty.DAG.md)
  :

  Transform a `DAG` object into a `tidy_dagitty` object

- [`do()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/do.md) :

  Pearls do-operator for `DAG` objects

- [`dag2matrix()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/dag2matrix.md)
  :

  Obtain a Adjacency Matrix from a `DAG` object

- [`matrix2dag()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/matrix2dag.md)
  :

  Obtain a `DAG` object from a Adjacency Matrix and a List of Node Types

## Select DAG Parameters

Automatically select suitable parameters in DAGs

- [`calibrate_dag()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/calibrate_dag.md)
  :

  Calibrate a partially specified `DAG` to match target values

- [`dag_from_data()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/dag_from_data.md)
  :

  Fills a partially specified `DAG` object with parameters estimated
  from reference data

## Simulation

Simulate data from a DAG and manipulate or visualize the output

- [`sim_from_dag()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/sim_from_DAG.md)
  :

  Simulate Data from a `DAG`

- [`sim_discrete_time()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/sim_discrete_time.md)
  :

  Simulate Data from a `DAG` with Time-Dependent Variables in Discrete
  Time

- [`sim_discrete_event()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/sim_discrete_event.md)
  :

  Simulate Data from a `DAG` with Time-Dependent Variables in Continuous
  Time

- [`sim_n_datasets()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/sim_n_datasets.md)
  :

  Simulate multiple datasets from a single `DAG` object

- [`sim2data()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/sim2data.md)
  [`as.data.table(`*`<simDT>`*`)`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/sim2data.md)
  [`as.data.frame(`*`<simDT>`*`)`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/sim2data.md)
  :

  Transform `sim_discrete_time` output into the start-stop, long- or
  wide-format

- [`plot(`*`<simDT>`*`)`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/plot.simDT.md)
  : Plot a Flowchart for a Discrete-Time Simulation

## Root nodes

Functions that can be used as root nodes

- [`rbernoulli()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/rbernoulli.md)
  : Generate Random Draws from a Bernoulli Distribution
- [`rcategorical()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/rcategorical.md)
  : Generate Random Draws from a Discrete Set of Labels with Associated
  Probabilities
- [`rsample()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/rsample.md)
  : Sample values from a given vector
- [`rconstant()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/rconstant.md)
  : Use a single constant value for a root node
- [`rtexp()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/rtexp.md) :
  Generate Data from a left-truncated exponential distribution

## Child nodes

Functions that can be used as child nodes

- [`node_gaussian()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/node_gaussian.md)
  : Generate Data from a (Mixed) Linear Regression Model
- [`node_binomial()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/node_binomial.md)
  : Generate Data from a (Mixed) Binomial Regression Model
- [`node_conditional_prob()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/node_conditional_prob.md)
  : Generate Data Using Conditional Probabilities
- [`node_conditional_distr()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/node_conditional_distr.md)
  : Generate Data by Sampling from Different Distributions based on
  Strata
- [`node_multinomial()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/node_multinomial.md)
  : Generate Data from a Multinomial Regression Model
- [`node_polr()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/node_polr.md)
  : Generate Data from an Ordered Logistic or Probit Regression
- [`node_poisson()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/node_poisson.md)
  : Generate Data from a (Mixed) Poisson Regression Model
- [`node_negative_binomial()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/node_negative_binomial.md)
  : Generate Data from a Negative Binomial Regression Model
- [`node_zeroinfl()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/node_zeroinfl.md)
  : Generate Data from a Zero-Inflated Count Model
- [`node_identity()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/node_identity.md)
  : Generate Data based on an expression
- [`node_mixture()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/node_mixture.md)
  : Generate Data from a Mixture of Node Definitions
- [`node_cox()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/node_cox.md)
  : Generate Data from a Cox-Regression Model
- [`node_aalen()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/node_aalen.md)
  : Generate Data from an Aalen Additive Hazards Model
- [`node_aftreg()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/node_rsurv.md)
  [`node_ahreg()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/node_rsurv.md)
  [`node_ehreg()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/node_rsurv.md)
  [`node_poreg()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/node_rsurv.md)
  [`node_ypreg()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/node_rsurv.md)
  : Generate Data from Parametric Survival Models

## Time-dependent nodes

Functions that can only be used as time-dependent nodes

- [`node_time_to_event()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/node_time_to_event.md)
  : Generate Data from repeated Bernoulli Trials in Discrete-Time
  Simulation
- [`node_competing_events()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/node_competing_events.md)
  : Generate Data with Multiple Mutually Exclusive Events in
  Discrete-Time Simulation
- [`node_next_time()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/node_next_time.md)
  : Generate the Next Time of an Event in Discrete-Event Simulation

## Misc

- [`long2start_stop()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/long2start_stop.md)
  :

  Transform a `data.table` in the long-format to a `data.table` in the
  start-stop format

- [`simDAG-package`](https://robindenz1.github.io/simDAG/reference/simDAG.md)
  : Simulate Data from a DAG and Associated Node Information
